$comment: flow: S8 item 2 (per-sink receipts; supersession and tombstones acknowledged per sink); item 4 (three independent facts, never conflated: a failed sink leaves publication partial and raises a capability incident, and neither undoes completion nor stops surveillance); §4.2 (dated capability facts that alert on the transition); §4.3 (silence is never success) | boundaries: Projector / publication; Station supervisor; Operator | design-review: §9 (per-sink delivery receipts, partial delivery recovery); §6 (an ambiguous outcome is a visible reconciliation state with an owner, never a silent park) | adjudication: (a)G-A1 | invariants: P-2; P-4; RG-3; RG-4; RG-U; L-4; H-2 | note: what a delivery result may say about the world, and nothing more. There is no completion field and no currency field in this document - a sink cannot report, and a reader cannot infer from a receipt, that a topic is complete or current
title: Export delivery receipt
description: One attempt to deliver one export manifest's bundle to one sink. Returned by `deliver(manifest, bundle)` and recorded by the projector; a retry is a new attempt with a new receipt, never an edit of an old one. The ordering pair (generation, options_revision) is carried so a receipt says which material this attempt was about: a sink that already accepted a higher pair reports `skipped_superseded` instead of overwriting. An attempt whose result is not known is `outcome_unknown` and must be reconciled — it is never read as delivered, never as failed, and never as a zero anywhere.

invocation_id.description: The invocation this delivery ran under, so one id threads the chain to the commit receipt (H-1).

status.description: delivered: the sink accepted the whole bundle and acknowledged the tombstones. failed: the attempt was refused or errored. skipped_superseded: the sink already holds a higher ordering pair, so this attempt correctly wrote nothing. outcome_unknown: the attempt's result is not established (the process died mid-delivery, the response was unreadable) and needs reconciliation before anything may be concluded from it.

written.description: How much of the bundle the sink took, as an observed count. A sink that stopped part-way reports `partial` with what it actually wrote, which is a lower bound and never a total; a sink whose outcome is unknown reports `unknown`. The one legitimate zero here is a deliberately skipped delivery, which is known to have written nothing.

error_class.description: A typed failure class, not a message: unreachable, auth_failed, refused (the sink rejected the payload), schema_mismatch (the destination does not match the export schema version), quota, timeout, partial_write, unreadable_response.

capability_fact_id.description: The dated capability fact this failure raised (`capability_facts.fact_id`). Required for a failure and for an unknown outcome: a dead export sink is a visible, dated incident with a since-time, which is the rule the 2026-09-21..24 secrets outage produced (H-2). It is never, by itself, a reason to block completion.

hold_id.description: The typed hold that owns getting this delivery finished, when one was raised (H-3: class, owner, deadline and what clears it live on the hold, not here).

allOf.description: Delivered means the sink said so: an acknowledgement time, the tombstones acknowledged, an observed count, no error and nothing left to reconcile.
A failure names its class and raises a dated capability fact; it has no acknowledgement time.
An unknown outcome must be reconciled, and may not claim a count it cannot know (L-4, RG-4). It is not a failure, so it does not carry an error class.
A skipped delivery is the one place a zero is knowledge: nothing was written, and that is observed, not unknown.
Reconciliation is only ever pending for an unknown outcome; a known result is not quietly left open.
